chapters.1.lds: The Church lesson reads these images as testimony that Christ lives and guides the Church. Why does the living speaker answer fear before giving the command to write?
chapters.1.summary: The book calls itself a revelation of Jesus Christ, sent to John. John writes to seven assemblies in Asia. He was on the island of Patmos because of God’s word. On the Lord’s day he hears a voice like a trumpet. He sees one like a son of man among seven golden lampstands. His eyes are like fire, and a sharp sword comes from his mouth. John falls at his feet like a dead man. The figure tells him to write, and says the lampstands are the seven assemblies.
chapters.2.lds: The selected Church lesson connects these distinct messages with Christ's knowledge of personal trials. Why does praise for endurance fail to remove the need for repentance?
chapters.2.summary: John writes four messages from Christ. Ephesus has worked hard and tested false apostles but has left its first love. Smyrna is poor and yet rich, and will suffer for ten days. Pergamum holds fast where Satan’s throne is, yet some hold the teaching of Balaam. Thyatira has love and service but tolerates a woman called Jezebel. Each message ends with a promise to the one who overcomes. Each tells those with ears to hear what the Spirit says.
chapters.3.lds: The selected Church lesson connects these promises with Christ's help in overcoming trials. How can a reputation for life or wealth conceal the condition the speaker names?
chapters.3.summary: John writes three more messages. Sardis has a name for being alive and is dead. A few there have not soiled their clothes. Philadelphia has little power, has kept Christ’s word, and has an open door. Laodicea is neither cold nor hot and will be spat out. It says it is rich, yet it is poor, blind, and naked. Christ counsels it to buy gold, white clothes, and eye salve from him. He stands at the door and knocks.
chapters.4.lds: Doctrine and Covenants 77:1 reads the sea of glass as the sanctified earth. Why do the elders surrender crowns while praising the source of created life?
chapters.4.summary: John sees a door open in heaven and is called up. One sits on a throne there and shines like jasper and sardius. A rainbow surrounds the throne. Twenty-four elders sit on thrones in white with golden crowns. Seven lamps burn, and a sea like glass lies before the throne. Four living creatures, like a lion, a calf, a man, and an eagle, never rest. They say, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty.” The elders fall down and cast their crowns before the throne.
chapters.5.lds: The selected Church lesson reads the sealed book through Christ's unique role in salvation. How does the Lamb's death explain worthiness to open the book?
chapters.5.summary: John sees a book in the right hand of the one on the throne. It is sealed with seven seals. An angel asks who is worthy to open it, and no one is found. John weeps. An elder says the Lion of the tribe of Judah has overcome. John looks and sees a Lamb standing as though it had been slain. The Lamb takes the book, and the creatures and elders sing a new song. Countless angels and every creature join the praise.
chapters.6.lds: The selected Church lesson connects opened seals with the Savior's authority. Why do the killed witnesses still ask how long judgment will wait?
chapters.6.summary: The Lamb opens six seals. A rider on a white horse goes out to conquer. A red horse takes peace from the earth, and a black horse brings scarce food. A pale horse carries Death, and Hades follows. At the fifth seal John sees under the altar those killed for God’s word. They are given white robes and told to rest a little longer. At the sixth seal the earth quakes and the sky rolls up. Kings and slaves hide and ask who is able to stand.
chapters.7.lds: The selected Church lesson studies this vision within the hope of lasting divine rule. Doctrine and Covenants 77:8–10 gives a later reading of this sealing. How do shelter and wiped tears answer the earlier question about standing?
chapters.7.summary: Four angels hold back the winds until God’s servants are sealed. John hears the number: 144,000, twelve thousand from each tribe of Israel. Then he sees a crowd no one can count, from every nation. They wear white robes and hold palm branches. They cry that salvation belongs to God and to the Lamb. An elder says they have come out of the great suffering. They washed their robes white in the Lamb’s blood. They will never hunger or thirst again.
chapters.8.lds: The selected Church lesson studies these trumpet scenes within the hope of lasting divine rule. Why do the saints' prayers appear before the trumpet judgments?
chapters.8.summary: The Lamb opens the seventh seal, and heaven is silent for half an hour. Seven angels receive seven trumpets. Another angel offers incense with the prayers of the saints at the golden altar. He fills the censer with fire and throws it to the earth. The first trumpet burns a third of the earth and trees. The second and third strike a third of the sea and the rivers. The fourth darkens a third of the sun, moon, and stars. An eagle cries woe for the three trumpets still to come.
chapters.9.lds: The selected Church lesson asks how lasting divine rule gives hope amid plagues. Why does destruction fail to produce repentance in the surviving people?
chapters.9.summary: At the fifth trumpet a star falls and opens the pit of the abyss. Smoke rises, and locusts come out with power like scorpions. They may not kill, but they torment people without God’s seal for five months. Their king is called Abaddon, or Apollyon. At the sixth trumpet four angels bound at the Euphrates are released. An army of horsemen kills a third of mankind with fire and sulfur. The survivors do not repent of idols. They do not repent of murders, sorceries, sexual immorality, or thefts.
chapters.10.lds: The selected Church lesson invites questions about these scenes within the hope of divine rule. Doctrine and Covenants 77:14 calls the little book a mission to gather Israel. How do sweetness and bitterness shape the renewed task of speaking prophecy?
chapters.10.summary: A mighty angel comes down wrapped in a cloud, with a rainbow on his head. He holds a little open book and stands on sea and land. Seven thunders speak, and John is told not to write their words. The angel swears that there will be no more delay. A voice tells John to take the book from the angel. The angel says it will taste sweet and turn the stomach bitter. John eats it, and it is so. He is told he must prophesy again about many peoples and kings.
chapters.11.lds: The selected Church lesson emphasizes the announcement of the Lord's lasting kingdom. Doctrine and Covenants 77:15 calls the two witnesses prophets of the last days. Why does the witnesses' restored life precede the announcement of lasting rule?
chapters.11.summary: John is given a reed to measure God’s temple. Two witnesses prophesy in sackcloth for 1,260 days. Fire comes from their mouths, and they can shut the sky. The beast from the abyss kills them, and their bodies lie in the street. People celebrate for three and a half days. Then the breath of life enters them, and they go up to heaven. An earthquake follows. The seventh trumpet sounds, and voices say the world’s kingdom has become the Lord’s.
chapters.12.lds: The selected Church lesson connects this victory with testimony and the Lamb's blood. How can continued earthly danger occur within the account of the dragon's defeat?
chapters.12.summary: A woman clothed with the sun cries out in labor. A great red dragon with seven heads waits to devour her child. Her son, who will rule the nations, is caught up to God. The woman flees to the wilderness. Michael and his angels fight the dragon and throw him down to the earth. A voice calls him the accuser and says the brothers overcame him. The dragon pursues the woman, and the earth helps her. He goes to make war on the rest of her offspring.
chapters.13.lds: The selected Church lesson compares the dragon's methods with the Lamb's response. How does control over buying and selling turn worship into coercion?
chapters.13.summary: A beast rises from the sea with ten horns and seven heads. The dragon gives it power, and one head has a healed death wound. The whole earth marvels and worships it. It speaks blasphemies and makes war on the saints for forty-two months. A second beast rises from the earth with two horns like a lamb. It works signs and makes people worship the first beast’s image. It puts a mark on the right hand or forehead of all. The number of the beast is 666.
chapters.14.lds: The selected Church lesson connects the angel's gospel with Restoration teaching and shared participation. How does following the Lamb differ from the beast's enforced worship?
chapters.14.summary: John sees the Lamb on Mount Zion with 144,000 who bear his name. They sing a new song and follow the Lamb wherever he goes. An angel flies with eternal good news for every nation. A second says Babylon has fallen. A third warns that those who worship the beast will drink God’s wrath. A voice blesses the dead who die in the Lord. One like a son of man reaps the earth’s harvest. An angel gathers the grapes and throws them into the winepress of God’s wrath.
chapters.15.lds: Why does the victors' song appear before the final plagues?
chapters.15.summary: John sees seven angels with the seven last plagues. Those who overcame the beast stand on a sea of glass mixed with fire. They hold harps of God. They sing the song of Moses and the song of the Lamb. The song says all nations will come and worship. The temple of the tabernacle of the testimony opens in heaven. One of the living creatures gives the angels seven golden bowls of wrath. Smoke fills the temple, and no one can enter until the plagues end.
chapters.16.lds: What does the warning about alertness require when it gives no date?
chapters.16.summary: A voice tells the seven angels to pour out the bowls. Sores, a sea of blood, and rivers of blood follow. The sun scorches people, and they blaspheme and do not repent. The beast’s kingdom is darkened. The Euphrates dries up for the kings from the east. Three unclean spirits like frogs gather the kings for war. The seventh bowl brings a voice saying, “It is done,” and a great earthquake. Great hail falls, and people blaspheme God.
chapters.17.lds: The selected Church lesson reads Babylon as a warning against the world's wickedness. How do the city's supporting rulers become agents of its destruction?
chapters.17.summary: An angel shows John a woman seated on a scarlet beast. She wears purple and gold and is drunk with the saints’ blood. Her name is “Babylon the Great.” The angel explains the mystery. The beast’s seven heads are seven mountains and seven kings. The ten horns are ten kings who give their power to the beast. They will make war on the Lamb, and he will overcome them. The horns will hate the woman, the great city, and burn her.
chapters.18.lds: The selected Church lesson connects departure from Babylon with refusing participation in wrongdoing. Why does leaving the city require refusing participation in its wrongdoing?
chapters.18.summary: An angel cries that Babylon the great has fallen. Another voice calls God’s people to come out of her. Her sins have reached heaven, and she will be repaid double. Kings who shared her luxury weep at the smoke of her burning. Merchants weep because no one buys their cargo. The list runs from gold and spices to the bodies and souls of people. Shipmasters cry out that such wealth was ruined in one hour. A mighty angel throws a millstone into the sea, and the city’s music stops.
chapters.19.lds: The selected Church lesson connects this vision with preparation for the Second Coming. How does wedding clothing differ from the city's purchased splendor?
chapters.19.summary: A great crowd in heaven praises God for judging the great prostitute. A voice announces the Lamb’s marriage, and his wife has made herself ready. John falls to worship the angel and is told to worship God. Heaven opens, and a rider called Faithful and True sits on a white horse. His robe is sprinkled with blood, and his name is the Word of God. A sword comes from his mouth. The beast and the false prophet are thrown into the lake of fire. The birds are called to feed on the armies.
chapters.20.lds: The selected Church lesson connects opened books with final judgment and present choices. How does judgment of great and small limit the apparent protection of power?
chapters.20.summary: An angel binds the dragon in the abyss for a thousand years. Those beheaded for the testimony of Jesus live and reign with Christ. This is called the first resurrection. After the thousand years Satan is released and gathers Gog and Magog. Fire devours them, and the devil is thrown into the lake of fire. John sees a great white throne. The dead are judged by what is written in the books. Death and Hades are thrown into the lake of fire, the second death.
chapters.21.lds: The selected Church lesson reads these promises through the hope of celestial glory. How does the descending city answer earlier accounts of loss and exploitation?
chapters.21.summary: John sees a new heaven and a new earth, and the sea is no more. The holy city, new Jerusalem, comes down from God like a bride. A voice says God’s dwelling is with people. The one on the throne says he is making all things new. An angel shows John the city, with twelve gates named for Israel’s tribes. Its twelve foundations bear the names of the Lamb’s apostles. The city is pure gold, and its gates are pearls. It has no temple or sun, for God and the Lamb light it.
chapters.22.lds: The selected Church lesson connects the opening river and light promises with celestial glory. How do freely offered water and faithful hearing belong together in the final invitation?
chapters.22.summary: The angel shows John the river of life flowing from the throne. The tree of life grows beside it, and its leaves heal the nations. God’s servants will see his face, and there will be no night. Jesus says he is coming soon. John falls before the angel and is again told to worship God. He is told not to seal the book, for the time is near. A warning forbids adding to or taking from the book’s words. The book ends with a prayer for the Lord Jesus to come.
